memories.content: The user's maternal aunt keeps one spare key to the user's home.
If the door is locked, the user is accustomed to contacting their maternal aunt, who has the spare key, before contacting building management.
When going to collect the spare key from their maternal aunt, the user wants to give an arrival time first so neither person has to wait.
The user feels at ease only after returning a borrowed spare key in person on the same day.
The user feels uneasy about writing down a new entrance passcode on paper.
The user found it difficult when a family member arrived without notice during a meeting and the user could not respond immediately.
On a day their younger brother received a package for them, the user felt reassured after checking the delivery photo.
The user's maternal aunt wants confirmation that the user is coming in person before handing over the spare key.
Confirm with the user before sharing the spare key's storage location or the maternal aunt's contact information.
The management office of a multi-unit residential building does not hold a unit key without verifying identity.
The user keeps waterproof shoes for rainy days to the left of the entrance.
On a day the user walked in the rain wearing thin shoes, their socks became wet and they changed them after arrival.
On the next rainy day, the user wore waterproof shoes and their feet remained dry.
On a day the user walked for a long time in new shoes, their heel chafed and they shortened the route home.
The user wore the same shoes on two short outings before using them on a long walk.
On a day the user dried an umbrella outside the entrance, they found it immediately before the next outing.
On a day the user put a folded wet umbrella in their bag, documents inside became wet.
When rain is forecast, the user's mother expects the user may forget an umbrella and sets out a spare at the entrance.
When proposing a long-distance walking plan, check both the weather that day and recent records of shoe discomfort.
Even if the local agent knows a shoe's location, it cannot know its current condition or whether it is usable.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate practical domains: the reference frame concerns home access, key handling, privacy, and related family coordination, while the compared frame concerns rainy-weather gear, footwear comfort, umbrella handling, and walking plans. No operational claim overlaps sufficiently for a cross-frame relation.
